articles.title: Updated Fantasy Football Rankings After the 2026 Preseason
articles.summary: One week. That's all that stands between us and the first game of the 2026 NFL season. When the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots kick off their Super Bowl LX rematch on Sept. 9, another fantasy football season will begin.
articles.body:
One week. That's all that stands between us and the first game of the 2026 NFL season. When the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots kick off their Super Bowl LX rematch on Sept. 9, another fantasy football season will begin.

That leaves one final draft weekend: One last chance for managers who have been drafting all summer, and the first opportunity for those who have waited until the last minute to assemble a roster for the season ahead.

The end of draft season is always exciting, nerve-wracking and a little sad.

We're here to build on that excitement, ease those nerves and dry those tears. You'll find a range of resources to help make your final draft of 2026 your best, including PPR rankings by position and overall, plus values and sleepers to target and busts to avoid.

Before we get to the position-by-position rankings, let's take a look at the draft-day landscape from 10,000 feet with a list of the top fantasy players overall in PPR leagues in 2026.

As we do, though, consider this piece of wisdom from the great philosopher Michael Gerard Tyson: "Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the mouth."

Follow this list blindly and take the highest-ranked player in every round, and you could run into trouble. Likewise, rigidly committing to a Zero RB approach without accounting for how the draft is unfolding can leave you at a disadvantage.

Stay alert: Draft flow and the approaches of other managers can significantly affect your decisions. Preparation is essential, but you must remain flexible when the draft does not unfold as expected.

Be ready, be flexible and remember the one principle that should guide you: value.

Quarterback is the most important position in the NFL. But that importance doesn't carry over into fantasy football.

This isn't to say elite signal-callers don't have value. But that value is muted by the high price tag it takes to acquire them in drafts. More often than not, the "edge" gained by drafting a high-end QB isn't worth the hole it leaves at running back or wide receiver.

The smart play at quarterback is patience. There are signal-callers available in the QB8-QB12 range with legitimate top-five upside, and you can be the last team in a 12-team league to draft a starter under center and still be fine.

Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars ( ADP : QB10)

Lawrence finished last year fourth among quarterbacks in fantasy points, and from Week 10 on he quietly led the position. The Jaguars have no shortage of passing-game weapons and Liam Coen's offense has produced back-to-back top-five finishes at quarterback. Three in a row is a real possibility.

Nix has shown no ill effects from the fractured ankle that ended his 2025 season. The Broncos added a high-end weapon in the offseason in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and Denver was quietly fourth in the league last year with 613 pass attempts. Nix was seventh in fantasy points among quarterbacks a year ago.

Allen is an example of why high-end fantasy quarterbacks aren't worth the high-end price tag. Yes, he was fantasy's highest scoring quarterback last year, but it was by less than a fantasy point per game over Matthew Stafford, who came off the board over 10 rounds later.

Joe Burrow, Cincinnati Bengals (ADP: QB3)

Burrow is the highest-ranked pure pocket passer in terms of average draft position—and that is not a good thing. For him to return value, he has to post ridiculous passing numbers a la two years ago. He also has a lengthy history and plays behind a sketchy offensive line.

Goff isn't an especially exciting fantasy option. He doesn't have any rushing upside. But he was second in the league in passing yards last year, is at the helm of one of the NFL's most prolific offenses and he hasn't finished lower than seventh in fantasy points among quarterbacks over the past three years.

Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings (ADP: QB17)

Murray won the starting job under center in the Twin Cities. The Vikings offense has plenty of weapons. Murray has demonstrated elite fantasy upside in the past. And we have already seen Kevin O'Connell have success with a reclamation project.

Whether you're an old-school fantasy drafter who likes to attack the running back position early or a Zero RB drafter who prefers to fade the position until the later rounds, there's one buzzword to remember where running backs are concerned: scarcity.

Running back is the shallowest position in fantasy football. In an era of committee attacks and muddied backfields, the number of every-down workhorses seemingly shrinks by the year.

Never mind the injuries that have already hit the position this year. Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty and Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love are already dealing with ankle injuries, with Love reportedly sidelined by a high ankle sprain. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner's Exempt List following an offseason arrest.

Proceed with caution: the backfield is full of potential pitfalls.

Kyren Williams, Los Angeles Rams (ADP: RB15)

Yes, Williams ceded some touches to Blake Corum over the second half of last season. But his efficiency numbers were better than in 2024, and his yardage and fantasy production remained essentially unchanged. Williams is going to post a fourth straight top-10 fantasy campaign—with an RB2 price tag in drafts.

Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans (ADP: RB30)

Pollard inspires little enthusiasm among fantasy drafters, but he's the unquestioned lead back for the Titans. Pollard and Derrick Henry of the Baltimore Ravens are the only two active running backs with four straight 1,000-yard seasons on the ground.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers (ADP: RB3)

McCaffrey was fantasy's highest-scoring running back last year, but there's zero chance he repeats that feat. He is a 30-year-old running back coming off a career-high 413 touches who missed 13 games both times he has come off a season with 2,000 total yards in his career.

Jeremiyah Love, Arizona Cardinals (ADP: RB13)

This analyst was already avoiding Love at his ADP because of concerns about the Cardinals' offense. Now, the third overall pick in April's draft enters his first professional season managing an ankle injury. With Tyler Allgeier also on the roster and $54 million in guaranteed money committed to their rookie runner, Arizona has ample reason to manage his workload carefully early in the season.

Chuba Hubbard, Carolina Panthers (ADP: RB36)

With Hubbard missing a chunk of camp and all of the preseason with a bad hamstring, many fantasy managers have anointed Jonathon Brooks the lead back in Carolina and written Hubbard off entirely. But Brooks has carried the ball all of nine time for 22 yards over two seasons in the NFL. He's also torn his ACL twice.

Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars (ADP : RB43)

The general consensus among fantasy managers is that Bhayshul Tuten is the running back to roster in fantasy leagues this year. But Rodriguez is a Liam Coen favorite who has averaged 4.6 yards per carry in his career. The backfield workload in Duval County could wind up being a lot closer to an even split.

The days of wide receivers as second-class citizens in fantasy football are over.

With more and more teams running pass-heavy schemes and sets with three or four wide receivers, the list of fantasy-relevant wideouts has grown.

Add in the prevalence of PPR scoring, and elite wideouts can throw down just as many points as their counterparts at running back. As a whole, wide receivers also have a lower bust rate.

Given those realities, many fantasy managers now swear by addressing the position early and often. But wide receiver is considerably deeper than running back. Once you get beyond the top 36 RBs, the drop-off becomes much steeper. At that point in the wide receiver rankings, though, there are still plenty of players who can help a fantasy team.

No position affords more flexibility than wide receiver. Take advantage of it.

Jaylen Waddle, Denver Broncos (ADP: WR20)

Waddle is one of this analyst's favorite wide receiver targets. He has demonstrated top-10 upside in the past and appears to have developed a quick rapport with quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle projects to be the Broncos' No. 1 receiver in 2026 and should outperform this draft cost by a wide margin.

Carnell Tate, Tennessee Titans (ADP: WR32)

It's understandable that fantasy mangers have some concerns about the passing attack in Tennessee after the team was 30th in the league in that regard a year ago. But Cam Ward showed an affinity for chucking the rock downfield as a rookie, and in 2026 those vertical targets are going to go to the fourth overall pick in April's draft.

Malik Nabers, New York Giants (ADP: WR12)

The fantasy ceiling with Nabers is sky-high—he was sixth in PPR points among wide receivers as a rookie. But while it looks like he will be a go for Week 1 after tearing his ACL last season, the lack of an offseason isn't going to help his chances of a fast start. He is being drafted far closer to his fantasy ceiling than his floor.

Rashee Rice, Kansas City Chiefs (ADP: WR13)

On a per-game basis, Rice has demonstrated elite fantasy upside. But he's also had all kinds of trouble staying in those games—he has missed an average of 11 games a season the past two years. Throw in Patrick Mahomes returning from an ACL tear, and Rice is a pass as a high-end fantasy WR2.

Stefon Diggs, Washington Commanders (ADP: WR41)

Diggs was quietly good for the New England Patriots and fantasy managers alike last year, catching 85 passes, topping 1,000 receiving yards and finishing inside the top-20 wide receivers in PPR points. Expecting a repeat is pushing the boundaries of optimism, but expecting cheap WR3 numbers isn't.

Jalen Coker, Carolina Panthers (ADP: WR54)

Coker's numbers over his first two seasons have been relatively modest, but the Panthers thought enough of him to offer a lucrative offseason extension. Carolina head coach Dave Canales has identified him as the team's No. 2 receiver. If Bryce Young takes a step forward in 2026, Coker could be one of the biggest beneficiaries.

Drafting a tight end in 2026 is like playing Let's Make a Deal : There are three doors to choose from. Fantasy managers just need to hope they find the Big Deal—and avoid getting zonked.

Door No. 1 is the elite options. They have a high ceiling, a relatively high floor and a high price tag to go along with it.

Door No. 2 is the Tier 2 tight ends—a handful of TEs who have the potential to crack the top tier but also face question marks. Lower prices. Higher risk.

Then there's Door No. 3: the late-round options outside the top 10. The upside is that if one of these tight ends hits, you can find excellent value. The downside is the uncertainty—drafting two may be prudent because none is a sure thing.

This analyst appears to be choosing Door No. 3 more often than not in 2026—and isn't sure that's a good idea.

Travis Kelce, Kansas City Chiefs (ADP: TE11)

Yes, Kelce is 73 years old. Or 36. Whatever. Yes, Kelce averaged a career-low 50.1 receiving yards per game in 2025. But even in that "down" season, he finished third among tight ends in PPR scoring. The last time Kelce did not finish as a top-five fantasy tight end was 2014.

Isaiah Likely, New York Giants (ADP: TE12)

After four years in Mark Andrews' shadow in Baltimore, Likely followed John Harbaugh to New York. When the targets were there for him with the Ravens, he showed legitimate top-five fantasy upside. And with Malik Nabers sitting much of the summer, Likely has had all sorts of time to build a connection with Jaxson Dart.

Trey McBride, Arizona Cardinals (ADP: TE2)

This isn't to say McBride shouldn't be the second tight end drafted. But as we have moved through the summer, all the value has been drained from his asking price—he's being drafted just a few spots after Brock Bowers now. McBride is going to regress after a historic 2025 campaign. The only question is by how much.

Harold Fannin Jr., Cleveland Browns (ADP: TE8)

Fannin had an outstanding rookie season, leading the Browns in receptions, receiving yards and touchdown catches while finishing sixth among tight ends in PPR scoring. However, Cleveland's offensive uncertainty is one of several factors that could make a repeat performance difficult.

Juwan Johnson, New Orleans Saints (ADP: TE16)

Johnson is generating little in the way of fantasy buzz this summer, but he quietly ranked inside the top five among tight ends in both receptions and receiving yards last year on the way to a ninth-place finish in fantasy points. With Jordyn Tyson out indefinitely, Johnson should see a robust target share early in the season.

TE Greg Dulcich, Miami Dolphins (ADP: TE26)

To be clear, Dulcich isn't an elite talent—he's never had even 425 receiving yards in a season. But someone is going to have to catch the ball in Miami this year, and he had a strong camp. This is a dart throw, but it could pay off if Dulcich starts piling up garbage-time stats.

Despite all protestations and proclamations that swear there is, there really isn't a "best" draft strategy.

Leagues can be won and lost in all sorts of ways. Fantasy managers need to choose a plan they are comfortable executing—and be ready to pivot when another manager disrupts it three rounds into the draft.

That's fantasy football. Flexibility is critical on draft day. Except where defenses and kickers are involved. There, the strategy is rigid: wait.

In the vast majority of fantasy leagues, there is no reason to draft a defense and a kicker before your final two picks—in that order.

For a defense, target a unit with one or two favorable early matchups. When the schedule becomes less favorable, turn to the waiver wire. For a kicker, take the best option available.

Jacksonville Jaguars Defense (ADP: DST10)

Again, the smart play with defenses is to target a good one with a plus matchup or two to open the season. The schedule admittedly stiffens for the Jaguars after the opener, but the NFL's No. 1 run defense from a year ago hosts a Browns team that fielded the league's second-worst scoring offense in 2025.

Cam Little, Jacksonville Jaguars (ADP: PK5)

There is no reason why Little shouldn't be the first kicker drafted, if only because it's just a joy to have the youngster on a fantasy roster. There's a lot to be said for the feeling you get when he lines up for a 62-yard attempt and you know he's going to punch it through halfway up the uprights.

Aaron Donald's return gives the Rams an even more formidable front after the team added edge rusher Myles Garrett and cornerback Trent McDuffie. Expectations for Los Angeles' defense are understandably high. However, its early schedule is challenging, with four 2025 playoff teams among its first five opponents.

Brandon Aubrey, Dallas Cowboys (ADP: PK1)

Aubrey is a fantastic kicker—he's been a Pro Bowler all three years in the NFL and never finished lower than third in fantasy points among kickers. But even in his first-place season at the position (2023), he outscored the 10th-ranked kicker by less than two points per game. There's no edge there. Just a wasted flier.

The Raiders defense was not especially good last season—to put it kindly. However, Las Vegas invested heavily in its front seven during free agency and retained edge rusher Maxx Crosby. More importantly for early-season streaming, the Raiders open against a Dolphins offense with significant questions entering 2026.

Chris Boswell, Pittsburgh Steelers (ADP: PK13)

Boswell is not the flashiest fantasy option, but he has been productive. As recently as 2024, no kicker scored more fantasy points. He also plays for an offense that should be competent, if not elite—the type of unit that can stall in the red zone and create frequent field-goal opportunities.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Every Division's 'Wild Card' for the 2026 NFL Season
articles.body:
You know the one: They could get hot and make a playoff run, but they could just as easily suffer a season-long meltdown resulting in a premium first-round pick.

The gap between the ceiling and floor is particularly large, often because of unknowns at quarterback, within the coaching staff, or throughout the core of the roster.

These are the teams that might play spoiler, but could just as easily see their own seasons spoiled well before Halloween.

The Ceiling: New Dolphins head coach/former Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley could immediately get into a groove with 27-year-old former third-round pick Malik Willis, who generated nine passing/rushing touchdowns to zero interceptions and posted a 134.6 passer rating in limited action the last two years in Green Bay. The result could be a competitive season and a wild-card opportunity for Miami.

The Floor: Saddled with arguably the least-talented pass-catching group in the NFL and stuck behind an offensive line riddled with question marks, Willis struggles mightily in his first sustained run as a starter as a rebuilding team hits rock bottom.

Spoiler Factor: Even with everything falling apart the last couple years, they've played the Bills tough. In their last three meetings, they're 1-2 with a plus-four scoring margin.

The Ceiling: This season could be to Deshaun Watson what 2010 was to Michael Vick. Vick had been a non-factor for several seasons in a row before winning Comeback Player of the Year in an oft-dominant age-30 campaign with the Eagles. The 30-year-old Watson certainly has the talent and finds himself in that spot now. He's surrounded by intriguing young talent, a revamped offensive line and a new-look coaching staff. Those are the ingredients for a surprisingly competitive season.

The Floor: Watson could just as easily fall on his face again, and that young offensive supporting cast may need time to grow in a new system. There are no guarantees with the line, and the defense will almost certainly struggle sans Myles Garrett. They could easily end up with the No. 1 overall pick.

Spoiler Factor: In the second half last season, they went 2-1 with a positive scoring margin within the division. They've generally played Baltimore, Pittsburgh and Cincinnati tough in recent years.

The Ceiling: They get a full season from the Daniel Jones who posted a 109.9 passer rating during a 7-1 start to the 2025 season. That and strong contributions from Jonathan Taylor, an underrated and talented receiving corps and an experienced offensive line could carry them to a division title.

The Floor: They get the version of Daniel Jones who posted an 84.2 passer rating as the team went 1-4 following that hot start—a stretch that ended with him tearing his right Achilles. If he cannot stay healthy, Indianapolis could get even less. Combined with an overall lack of oomph on either side of the ball, that could leave the Colts fighting the Titans for third place in the division.

Honorable Mention in the Division: Speaking of the Titans, they were a respectable 2-3 from the start of December onward last season as top pick Cam Ward put up six touchdowns to zero interceptions and posted a 103.8 passer rating in his final four starts as a rookie. Could a new coaching staff maintain that trajectory? Or is this still a full-on rebuild that will require at least another roller-coaster of a season?

The Ceiling: We've seen it. It remains Super Bowl-high so long as Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid are cooking.

The Floor: We got a glimpse in 2025. If a 30-year-old Mahomes can't stay healthy and regain some of the magic from his 20s despite a significantly weaker supporting cast, the Chiefs will have an extremely difficult time hanging with the Broncos and Chargers.

Honorable Mention in the Division: There's no denying that the Raiders, who have invested considerable draft capital the last few offseasons and spent huge in free agency this spring, have plenty of talent in key spots. If they could catch fire with Kirk Cousins or Fernando Mendoza, they could remarkably send the Chiefs to the AFC West basement and hang with the Broncos and Chargers. Or it could be a total mess as the rebuild trudges on.

The Ceiling: There's a world in which Jaxson Dart takes off in his second season and becomes a star with top-notch support from an exciting skill-position group, a promising offensive line, a defense that features massive talent up front and an incoming head coach with Super Bowl pedigree. In that world, the Giants can shock the unpredictable NFC East.

The Floor: Ultimately, it remains low with so many questionable variables. The sample is small for Dart, and two key cogs (Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo) are coming back from major injuries. If the Eagles are the Eagles, a better defense helps Dallas bounce back, and Washington can rediscover what got it to the NFC title game in 2024, the Giants could be in for a third consecutive last-place campaign.

Spoiler Factor: At home in 2025, the Giants beat the Eagles and Cowboys by a combined margin of 68-34.

The Ceiling: They won 14 games in 2024. The core remains similar, but with wild-card Kyler Murray at quarterback. If Murray can stay healthy and produce to his talent level, the sky (or a surprise NFC North crown) is the limit for a team with a superstar receiver, a stacked offensive line and a high-quality defense.

The Floor: Murray reproduces the uneven form he showed over his final four seasons in Arizona, missing at least six games in three campaigns and posting a mediocre 90.3 passer rating overall. If a new environment cannot reignite the former No. 1 overall pick and J.J. McCarthy cannot provide a viable alternative, Minnesota is a .500-ish team at best.

Spoiler Factor: The Vikings finished the 2025 season on a five-game winning streak despite issues at quarterback. That run included multi-score victories over division rivals Detroit and Green Bay, as the team went 4-2 against the NFC North for the second consecutive season.

The Ceiling: If Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can deliver, the Falcons could prevail in the wide-open NFC South behind Bijan Robinson, who is in his prime, a fresh coaching staff, a solid offensive line and a budding defense.

The Floor: Tagovailoa may have peaked several years ago, while Penix may have peaked in the Pac-12. If so, there's only so much Robinson and a decent skill-position corps can do for a team that will likely still struggle defensively as well. They can wind up with seven or eight wins for a sixth season in a row.

Honorable Mention in the Division: Tyler Shough had a triple-digit passer rating in the final four weeks of his rookie season for a Saints squad that finished 4-1. That momentum and a sneaky-solid offseason could take New Orleans back to the top of the division. However, they're less than a sophomore slump away from a return to the basement.

The Ceiling: A similar 49ers core lost the Super Bowl by a field goal a few years ago, so San Francisco's ceiling entering 2026 is clearly championship level. Imagine what this experienced, well-coached and deeply talented team could accomplish if it simply stays healthy.

The Floor: Another injury-plagued campaign likely means another third-place finish when you're dealing with the Super Bowl favorite (Los Angeles) and the defending Super Bowl champion (Seattle).

Spoiler Factor: They beat both the Rams and Seahawks on the road in 2025. In fact, they haven't lost a regular-season game in Seattle since 2021.

articles.title: “There’s still parts of my brain I’m trying to rewire”: Puka Nacua’s ex GF Hallie Aiono opens up about psychiatrist visit after four-year relationship and alleged abuse
articles.summary: NFL News: It’s not easy to open up about loving someone for four years – the kind of love you felt in your bones. It’s not easy to publicly admit that the perso.
articles.body: It’s not easy to open up about loving someone for four years – the kind of love you felt in your bones. It’s not easy to publicly admit that the person you once loved made you feel extreme betrayal, abuse, and neglect, leaving you feeling crushed and as though your brain chemistry had been altered.It’s not easy to meet with a psychiatrist and revisit some of the darkest days of your life.It’s not easy to share a child with someone you believe caused so much pain and then still hope for a normal life, a healthy love, and a brighter future with an open heart and an open mind after everything you have been through.But Puka Nacua’s ex-girlfriend, Hallie Aiono, is trying. Trying with all her might -for herself, for her son Kingston, and for the future she hopes to build for her future children.Puka Nacua’s ex-girlfriend Hallie Aiono opens up about her psychiatrist visit and mental health journeyOpening up about mental health is rarely easy, particularly when the experiences behind those struggles are profoundly personal. Hallie Aiono, the former girlfriend of Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, has shared a candid update about her decision to meet with a psychiatrist.Aiono, who shares a son, Kingston, with Nacua, said she has spent the past year and a half working through some of the most difficult experiences of her life.She revealed that she would soon be meeting with a psychiatrist, admitting that discussing mental health publicly makes her uncomfortable.For years, Aiono feared receiving a mental health “label,” believing that asking for help meant she was weak or that something was wrong with her. Her perspective, however, has gradually changed.Aiono explained that she has experienced anxiety for as long as she can remember and has also gone through periods of depression. She expressed curiosity about whether ADHD [Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder] or OCD [Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder] could help explain some of the ways her mind works.Above all, Aiono said she wants to understand herself better and become “the healthiest version” of herself.However, her willingness to discuss intensely personal struggles is not entirely new. During her pregnancy, Aiono previously shared candid posts about body dysmorphia and her changing relationship with her appearance [3 months pregnancy look compared to 9 months pregnancy look].Hallie Aiono reflects on four-year relationship and alleged abuseThe most emotional part of Aiono’s message centered on a previous four-year relationship [supposedly with Puka Nacua] and the drastic change she experienced after loving someone completely.Aiono alleged that she went from feeling intensely connected to her former partner to experiencing “extreme betrayal, abuse” and “complete neglect.” While some portions of her personal life became public, she said the experiences that happened away from public view [probably behind closed doors] affected her most profoundly.She said those experiences “completely crushed” her and left her feeling as though her brain chemistry had been altered.Although Aiono said she has made significant progress over the past year and a half, she admitted some of the emotional effects remain, and she still needs to rewire them.“Right now, I’m just really trying to understand myself,” Aiono said in the TikTok video.“Understand why my brain works the way it works. Why I react the way I react. I’m just trying to find the healthiest version of myself, especially after the past year and a half.”She added, “I’ve talked about it on here a few other times, but I have experienced the darkest, darkest days of my life in the past year and a half, and I have healed so much. I really have. But I also feel like there’s still parts of my brain that I’m trying to rewire.”These are Aiono’s allegations and descriptions of her own experiences. She has previously made public accusations and shared critical posts regarding Nacua during her pregnancy and amid their highly publicized personal and legal disputes. She reportedly labeled him a “narcissist,” too.Puka Nacua’s ex Hallie Aiono wants a healthier future for her son KingstonFor Aiono, meeting with a psychiatrist appears to be about more than finding answers about anxiety or depression. She said she wants to better understand herself and learn how to move forward without letting past experiences dictate what she believes love should look or feel like.Motherhood is also a crucial part of her motivation. Aiono said she wants to become the best version of herself for Kingston and for any future children she may have.By speaking openly about her fears surrounding psychiatric care, Aiono turned a profoundly personal moment into a powerful message for others who may also feel afraid to seek help: asking for support is not a sign of weakness.For Aiono, taking that first step appears to be part of the healthier future she says she wants to build - both for herself and for her son.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Discusses 'Magical' Taylor Swift Wedding, 'So Thankful for Everybody'
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce discussed his recent wedding with pop star Taylor Swift on the latest edition of the New Heights podcast, which dropped Wednesday.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce discussed his recent wedding with pop star Taylor Swift on the latest edition of the New Heights podcast, which dropped Wednesday.

During a conversation with his brother, former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, Travis showed his appreciation for the guests and everyone who made it a special night for him and Taylor (beginning at the 11:37 mark of the podcast) .

"Me and Taylor are so thankful for everybody that showed up, from the vows to just seeing everyone, to how much fun we had, throughout the entire evening and hearing that, kind of be relayed through everybody's stories of the night," Kelce said. "And it was just so magical, man."

Kelce went on to note that he wished the wedding "could have lasted even longer than it did," because of the enjoyable time that was had by all.

The wedding took place at Madison Square Garden in New York City on July 3, and Kelce explained that he and Swift chose the unique venue because they wanted to get married "somewhere where we could have a very intimate and genuine setting without a lot of distractions."

Kelce expressed his gratitude to MSG for delivering on what they wanted, and he also gave a "special thank you" to actor Adam Sandler, who officiated the wedding.

Now, Kelce is deep in preparations for the start of his 14th NFL season, all of which have been spent in Kansas City.

An 11-time Pro Bowler, four-time First Team All-Pro and three-time Super Bowl champion, Kelce is already widely regarded as one of the greatest tight ends in NFL history and a future Pro Football Hall of Famer.

There were plenty of rumors and speculation that he would retire after the 2025 season, but he is back for at least one more campaign, as he looks to help the Chiefs get back to the playoffs after falling short last season.

articles.title: Predicting Every Game of the 2026 NFL Season: NFC South
articles.summary: If you’re trying to predict an NFL team’s end-of-season record, the wrong way to do it is to bring up the schedule and pick results of each game. You simply...
articles.body:
If you're trying to predict an NFL team's end-of-season record, the wrong way to do it is to bring up the schedule and pick results of each game. You simply can't hope to predict stuff that well, and you'd be better served finding a method that assigns a percent chance of winning each game, adding up those percentages and converting it to a win/loss record. Going game-by-game is silly.

Because of that opening paragraph, what follows isn't betting advice . It is just a look at the schedule for each NFL team in 2026 and how things might shape up for them this season. Below, check out the 2026 week-by-week results for each NFL team with some thoughts on their outlook.

NFC South below. All odds cited are per DraftKings Sportsbook.

Game-by-Game Results for 2026: NFC South

The Falcons get off to a good start to their 2026 season.

It's 2-0 for Atlanta. First time since 2023, only the second since 2017.

Atlanta gets its first loss of the season in Green Bay.

The Saints pull the Falcons back to .500.

Remember when the Falcons said they weren't going to pursue Lamar Jackson? I bet he does.

And with this, the formerly 2-0 Falcons fall to 2-5.

Atlanta finally gets another win by beating the Bucs.

Atlanta over Kansas City in the Tony Gonzalez Bowl.

The Falcons travel to Minnesota and get a post-bye win.

Make it three straight for the Falcons and they're back to 6-6.

The Browns take down whoever is under center for Atlanta by this point.

On the road at Washington, another loss.

That's two five-game losing streaks for Atlanta in 2026, with a 6-1 record otherwise.

After a surprise playoff berth last year, Carolina starts slow in 2026.

Make it 0-2 for the defending NFC South champions.

The Panthers get on the board at Cleveland.

It's two in a row for the Panthers with a surprise win over Detroit.

After a bye, the Panthers fall in Philadelphia.

The Panthers take down the Buccaneers at home.

Once again, the Panthers surprise the Packers.

The Broncos have a tough time taking down the Panthers.

Carolina travels to New Orleans and beats the Saints.

Baltimore has an easy time taking down Carolina.

Tampa takes down Carolina, and the Panthers fall to 5-6.

Brian Flores' defense beats up on the powerless Panthers.

That's five straight losses for Carolina.

Seven straight losses for the Panthers after starting 5-4.

It's a meaningless win, but at least it's a win to close the season.

That's 0-2 for the Saints, but it's two tough matchups on the road.

Shough gets his first win of the season against the hapless Raiders.

Back to .500 with a home win over the Falcons.

The Saints got their first win of 2025 over the Giants, but they lose this time.

At least we can trust the French to more or less pronounce "Etienne" correctly, right?

Once again, the Saints are back to .500.

New Orleans takes down Carolina in a home game.

Through Week 11, the Saints will be alternating two-game winning and losing streaks.

Loser of this game has to give up "Who Dey" or "Who Dat" for life.

The Packers beat the Saints to end the two-game trend.

It's clearly the Bucs or the Saints for NFC South supremacy at this point, and the Bucs take the early lead.

The Cardinals surprise the Saints to put their backs against the wall.

The Saints get the 2026 sweep over Atlanta.

New Orleans beats Tampa to finish off the season.

Tampa starts with a loss against a strong Cincinnati offense.

Facing the Browns is a good way to get your first win of the season.

The two bays faced off a bunch in the early 2020s, but this is their first time since 2023.

Back-to-back wins over the Packers and Cowboys gets the Bucs excited.

The Steelers kill the good vibes in Tampa.

A trip to Chicago yields the Bucs' fourth straight loss.

Tampa hosts the Chargers, but Los Angeles comes out on top.

The Ravens have an easy time against Tampa.

The Bucs take the edge in the NFC South race.

Here's the clutch move. It's a must-win victory over an elite team.

articles.title: 5 offenses to avoid in 2026 fantasy football drafts, including Falcons
articles.summary: These offenses aren't capable of producing consistent fantasy production
articles.body:
Fantasy football is about the players you don't take as much as the players who do land on your roster. Strategically avoiding the inevitable busts each season is a reliable way to win a spot in championship week, but it's easier said than done.

Injuries, scheme or coaching changes and roster turnover can make a player who excelled one season an afterthought the next. That's why identifying fantasy-friendly teams can be a valuable exercise in the draft process.

Good teams typically have less year-over-year change, and even while a coordinator may leave for a head coaching job, organizational stability built through winning should keep things running as normal -- usually with an established quarterback in place.

Bad teams, on the other hand, are defined by chaos, usually with a new coach, quarterback -- or both -- trying to figure it out on the fly. Here are five teams that fit the bill, meaning you should avoid targeting their players in 2026 fantasy drafts.

Bijan Robinson is widely considered a top-five pick in fantasy drafts with Drake London not far behind as a fringe first-rounder. Both should be avoided at cost, as the Falcons' quarterback situation is possibly the NFL's worst with a clearly past-his-prime Tua Tagovailoa battling the oft-injured Michael Penix Jr. This offense will make you pull your hair out.

The Browns are starting Deshaun Watson after two Achilles tears, have their worst offensive line in years and play in largely awful weather for the second half of the season. Those factors are enough to fade an otherwise promising skill group consisting of tight end Harold Fannin Jr., running back Quinshon Judkins, and wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Check back in on the Browns when they have an exciting young quarterback next year.

Reports out of training camp suggest Cam Ward isn't taking the second-year leap many were expecting, plus top-five pick Carnell Tate has been invisible in the preseason. With a below-average offensive line and a new coaching staff in place around them, this is an offense worth monitoring for 2027 but fading this year.

First-year coach Mike LaFleur stupefyingly gave first-round pick Jeremiyah Love 14 carries in his preseason debut, and now the star running back is battling a high ankle sprain with the season approaching. Oh, and garbage time king Jacoby Brissett, a bottom-five starting QB, held the team hostage over contract negotiations and missed much of the offseason program. This team is a complete mess that has a better chance of getting the No. 1 pick than helping you in fantasy.

The vibes surrounding Jayden Daniels have been horrendous ever since the No. 5 controversy emerged at LSU. Add in left tackle Laremy Tunsil's season-ending injury, an aging receiver group and possibly the NFL's least talented running back room, and there's not many reasons for optimism for this unit. An injury to Daniels, who was limited to seven games last year, could make every Commanders fantasy option unplayable.

articles.title: All-New 2026 College Football Week 1 QB Rankings: Where Does Arch Manning Land in Our Top 10?
articles.summary: Similar to the NFL, a gifted quarterback can turn a college football program into a playoff contender. This season’s crop […]
articles.body:
Similar to the NFL, a gifted quarterback can turn a college football program into a playoff contender. This season's crop of QB talent is filled with players who should hear their names called in Rounds 1 and 2 of the 2027 NFL Draft . But which signal callers stand above the rest as the best of the best entering the new season?

We look to answer that question with our brand new rankings of the top 10 QBs heading into Week 1 of the 2026 college football season.

There was a lot of buzz about South Carolina's Lanorris Sellers before last season because he was coming off a breakout campaign in 2024, when he tossed for 2,534 yards, ran for 674 and had 25 total TDs as a sophomore. Unfortunately, he and the Gamecocks took a disappointing step backward last year.

If South Carolina can be more like the team they were two years ago, Sellers definitely has the talent to become a household name in 2026.

Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and his staff worked their magic with Cal transfer Fernando Mendoza last year. Turning him into the latest Heisman winner and the leader of a team that brought the school its first football national title. They are hoping to do it again in 2026, this time with former TCU star Josh Hoover.

The senior had two rock-solid seasons for the Horned Frogs in 2024 and 2025. Peaking with a career-best 29 TDs last year. However, he also had a career-high 13 INTs. If he can cut down on his mistakes, he has the talent and support around him to be an elite QB all season.

Outside of Miami landing Mensah, Lane Kiffin making Sam Leavitt his first starting QB at LSU was one of the top stories that came out of the transfer portal in the spring. Heading into the 2025 season, the former Arizona State QB was on a lot of early Heisman candidate lists. However, a Lisfranc injury limited him to just seven games last year.

Not only is Leavitt dangerous in the passing game, but he can also put the ball down and make plays with his feet. He will have even better weapons around him in Baton Rouge and can end up in the Heisman conversation again as the year progresses.

Being the starting QB for an iconic program like Notre Dame comes with a lot of pressure. The type of pressure freshmen are not usually ready for. However, CJ Carr won the QB1 job last summer and was impressive in his first year as a starter in South Bend.

The youngster posted 2,741 passing yards, with 24 TDs to 6 INTs, and a noteworthy 168.1 passer rating. While he lost a pair of great running backs to the NFL, he continues to have his name thrust into the Heisman conversation because of the expectation that 2026 will be a breakout year for Carr.

Trinidad Chambliss was one of the best stories in college football last year. The junior college star lost the QB1 battle in camp to Austin Simmons. However, Simmons suffered a serious injury in Ole Miss' Week 2 game against Kentucky . Thrusting Chambliss into the starting role for a significant amount of time. Well, he never gave Simmons a chance to get the job back.

The senior threw for nearly 4,000 yards, ran for over 500 more, and posted 30 total TDs to 3 INTs last season. His strong showing in the playoffs only added to his legend, and it likely played a role in Mississippi judicial officials granting him another year of eligibility in 2026.

Oregon QB1 Dante Moore has put himself in an interesting position. He likely would have been at least the No. 2 pick in April's NFL Draft but chose to return for another season in Eugene. That was not planned, so the Ducks added former Nebraska starter Dylan Raiola in the transfer portal. It puts unexpected pressure on the junior because a talented QB is waiting in the wings.

However, if Moore takes another step forward in 2026 like he did last year when he threw for over 3,500 yards, 30 touchdowns, and hit on 71.8 percent of his passes, he should be just fine. While the Oregon QB tailed off late last year, he is getting a lot of Heisman buzz heading into this season.

A case can be made that Texas QB Arch Manning is the most famous player in college football right now. But it's not because he was amazing in his first year as a starter in 2025. It's because he has two former NFL stars as uncles, and he was the most hyped high school player of the decade two years ago.

However, he did perform well as a sophomore last year despite sky-high expectations. Throwing for 3,163 yards, ran for 399 more, with 36 total TDs and 7 INTS. If Manning can cut down on his mistakes and be more accurate, the talent is there to be in the conversation as the best player in the nation this season.

One of the biggest signings in the transfer portal this spring was Miami replacing Carson Beck with Duke star Darian Mensah. The former Blue Devils QB had a dynamite year in his lone season at Durham as he finished second in the nation in passing yards (3,973) and touchdowns (34).

If he can put up those numbers at Duke, with even better talent around him at the U, Mensah is primed to become a household name and Heisman Trophy finalist this year.

Ohio State's Julian Sayin had big shoes to fill last season. Will Howard wasn't one of the best QBs in the country when he started for the Buckeyes in 2024. But he did something many of his predecessors didn't by helping lead OSU to a national title. Yet, despite the high expectations as the QB1 for a program looking to repeat as champs, Sayin delivered in 2025.

The first-time starter posted 3,610 yards through the air with 32 TDs and 8 INTs. He was also one of the most efficient passers in the country. Tallying a 77.0 completion percentage last year. Sayin has all the skills and the talent around him to put up big numbers again against tough competition in 2026.

When healthy, USC's Jayden Maiava is one of the most dangerous passers in the country. He showed that last season when the Trojans star posted 3,711 passing yards with 24 touchdowns to 10 interceptions.

The QB has a quick release and may be the best deep ball thrower in the nation. Maiava's biggest issue has been his riskiness with the ball. But in his 2026 debut, he showed the peaks of his talent by hitting on 25 of 29 passes for 286 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions against San Jose State .

articles.title: Ryan Poles explains where Bears QB Caleb Williams has grown most
articles.summary: Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles discussed how head coach Ben Johnson has helped quarterback Caleb Williams get the joy back in his game.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have an opportunity to build off their success last year, reaching the NFC Divisional playoff round, sparked in a major way by the growth and play of quarterback Caleb Williams.

In his second season in the NFL, Williams had a brand new system led by head coach Ben Johnson, which saw the quarterback set a franchise record for most passing yards in a single season while leading a top-10 offense, but there's still plenty of room to grow.

On Tuesday, general manager Ryan Poles spoke about the trajectory of Williams' career as heads into Year 3 in the NFL, believing that the connection he's built with his head coach is key to long-term success.

Chicago Bears 53-man roster for 2026 season

"I think you see that joy back in his game where he's playing free," Poles said about the growth in his young quarterback. "I think he sees and identifies where he comes up short faster than what he did before, and I think that's where him and Ben (Johnson) are continuing to work really well together, trying to get better every single day."

There's no question that at least in the first year of their relationship, the Bears are getting what they had hoped for in the head coach-quarterback relationship, and now they'll look to build off of that first year success. If Williams can continue to make leaps in his game and development, not only will he be a highly-successful quarterback in the NFL, but he'll be the franchise cornerstone that the Bears have needed for decades.

articles.title: 11 days till Arizona Cardinals' opener: Remembering the 2011 season
articles.summary: With 11 days until the Arizona Cardinals' 2026 opener, let's look back at their 2011 season.
articles.body:
We continue the countdown to the start of the Arizona Cardinals ' regular season. Today, Wednesday, September 2, is 11 days away from the Arizona Cardinals' regular-season opener on Sept. 13 on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers.

With 11 days until Week 1, let's look back at the 2011 season for the Cardinals.

A look back at the 2011 season for the Cardinals

In 2011, we had to endure the NFL lockout. During the offseason, the Cardinals, reeling from Kurt Warner's decision to retire after 2009 and having suffered a 5-12 2010 season, they traded for quarterback Kevin Kolb in exchange for cornerback Domonique Rodgers-Cromartie and a second-round pick.

Kolb struggled with injuries. He suffered turf toe and had a concussion, only starting nine games. After a 1-6 start, they won five of their final six games to finish 8-8. Second-year quarterback John Skelton went 5-2 as a starter, and that triggered a QB competition for the following offseason.

Rookie cornerback Patrick Peterson, the fifth overall pick in the draft, returned four punts for touchdowns.

CB Patrick Peterson (as a punt returner)

Peterson was a first-team All-Pro, too. Fitzgerald made the second team.

Kolb had the most passing yards with 1,955, nine touchdowns and eight interceptions. Skelton passed for 1,913 yards and 11 touchdowns, but he threw 14 picks.

Running back Beanie Wells had 1,047 rushing yards to lead the team. Fitzgerald had 80 catches for 1,411 yards and eight touchdowns.

Calais Campbell led the Cardinals with eight sacks. Richard Marshall's three interceptions on defense led the team, and five players had at least 10 pass breakups, led by Wilson's 14.
